transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Mbeki, thank you for meeting with me. I need to discuss your CT scan results with you and correct some information you were given earlier.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope this is good news. The other doctor told me the scan was clear and I'd probably be going home today.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is actually why I am here. I have to tell you that the initial information was wrong. There was an error. The scan actually showed a pulmonary embolism, which is a blood clot in your lung.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A what? I don't understand. You just said it was clear.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is confusing and frustrating. A pulmonary embolism is when a clot travels to the lung and blocks blood flow. This was visible on the images, but the first radiology report missed it. Because of that mistake, we didn't start your treatment for eighteen hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Eighteen hours. You're telling me I've been sitting here for nearly a day with a clot in my lung because someone missed it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly what happened. I am very sorry. Our team failed to catch this in a timely manner, and we take full responsibility for that delay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't afford to be in here for a day, let alone more. I have a business to run. I told the other doctor my shop is short-staffed. Now you're telling me I'm sicker than I thought?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It sounds like the stress of your business is weighing on you right now, and adding this medical uncertainty on top of that is incredibly overwhelming.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's more than overwhelming. It's a waste of my time. If this was caught yesterday, would I even be here now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a fair question. While we can't change the timing, we can focus on getting the treatment right now. Just to make sure I've explained this clearly, can you tell me what your understanding is of what went wrong with the scan?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You missed a clot. The report was wrong. I waited eighteen hours for a treatment I should have had yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct. Does that make sense, or is there any part of the medical side that is still unclear?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, that part is clear. I'm just wondering why this happens. This is a hospital.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand why you're questioning our competence. It is unacceptable that this was missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I have people counting on me. If I'm out for another week, I'm losing money. I'm losing clients.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how much pressure you're under with your business. It's not just about the health risk, but the real financial hit this takes when you're the one keeping everything running.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Exactly. So what now? When do I get out of here?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are starting the blood thinners now. We'll monitor you for a while.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: For how long? I need a date.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just see how you respond to the medication. We'll keep an eye on your oxygen and your heart rate.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a date. Is it two days? Three?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a specific day right now. We'll just stay tuned to see how the meds work.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is exactly what I'm talking about. Everything is vague. Yesterday it was "going home today," now it's "we'll see."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is unsettling, but we have to be cautious. Let's just move on to the next part of the check-up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not moving on until I know how this affects my discharge.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just wait and see how the blood thinners go. I'll check in with you later.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language at the end of the encounter ('Let's just move on to the next part of the check-up').

E.justification: The error (pulmonary embolism/missed report) is named in the second turn, lay language is used, and comprehension is checked twice ('can you tell me what your understanding is', 'is there any part... still unclear').

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language ('I am very sorry'), takes full team responsibility, and maintains this accountability under pushback.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('confusing and frustrating', 'overwhelming') and references the patient's specific concerns regarding his business and financial hit.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders and vague responses regarding the timeline ('we'll just see', 'stay tuned', 'I can't give you a specific day').
